record.paper_title: Approximation by rational functions: Open problems.
record.context_brief: Pole locations of best rational approximants
record.original_question: For the rational functions of best approximation appearing in the Padé-style table R_{mn}, determine the location and distribution of their poles. More specifically, the source notes that several results related to the Padé table and to these best rational approximants are known, but the basic problem of identifying where the poles of the best approximants lie remains open.

evidence.page: zbMATH review text, final sentence of main summary paragraph
evidence.quote: Still other results connected with the Pade table and (*) are known; in each case the problem remains unsolved: Where are the poles of the rational functions of best approximation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f$ be a continuous real-valued function on the interval $[-1,1]$. For nonnegative integers $m$ and $n$, let $\mathcal{R}_{m,n}$ denote the set of rational functions $r=p/q$ with real coefficients, where $p$ is a polynomial of degree at most $m$ and $q$ is a polynomial of degree at most $n$, with $q$ not identically zero. By a classical theorem, there exists a unique rational function $r_{m,n}^*\in\mathcal{R}_{m,n}$ that minimizes the uniform error
$$\|f-r\|_{[-1,1]}=\sup_{x\in[-1,1]}|f(x)-r(x)|$$
over all $r\in\mathcal{R}_{m,n}$. Call $r_{m,n}^*$ the best rational approximant of type $(m,n)$ to $f$, and arrange these into the table $R=(r_{m,n}^*)_{m,n\ge 0}$.

Problem: Describe, for a general continuous (or sufficiently smooth) function $f$ on $[-1,1]$, the location in the complex plane of the poles of $r_{m,n}^*$ as $(m,n)$ varies. In particular, determine the asymptotic distribution of the poles of $r_{m,n}^*$ along rays of the table (e.g.\ as $m,n\to\infty$ with $m/n$ tending to a fixed ratio), identifying where the poles cluster, whether they remain bounded away from $[-1,1]$, and how their distribution relates to the analytic properties of $f$.
artifact.status_search_result: For specific classes of functions—most notably $f(x)=|x|^\alpha$ on $[-1,1]$ and functions with fast rational approximability—the asymptotic distribution of poles of best rational approximants has been determined (Stahl and others). For nonholomorphic $f\in C[-1,1]$ with bounded denominator degree, the zero/pole distribution is governed by the equilibrium measure of $[-1,1]$. However, for general continuous functions and for general ray sequences in the table, the question of where the poles lie remains without a complete answer; the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Poles and zeros of best rational approximants of |x|
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic distribution of poles and zeros of best rational approximants to |x| on [-1,1] is determined.
status_evidence.claim: Pole distribution is known for f(x)=|x|.

status_evidence.title: Distribution of poles of diagonal rational approximants to functions of fast rational approximability
status_evidence.snippet: Most poles of diagonal best rational approximants to functions admitting fast rational approximation leave the region of meromorphy.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results are known for highly approximable functions.

status_evidence.title: On the Distribution of Zeros and Poles of Rational Approximants on Intervals
status_evidence.snippet: For nonholomorphic f, with bounded denominator degree, zero distribution governed by equilibrium measure of [-1,1].
status_evidence.claim: Distribution results exist under restricted denominator degree.
